decisive_items: irregularly enhancing mass in the right ear canal, middle ear cavity, and mastoid air cells
erosive changes of the skull base and extension into the right middle cranial fossa
response.rationale: Irregular enhancing mass with skull base erosion and intracranial extension, plus profound sensorineural hearing loss, strongly favor a malignant middle ear neoplasm over benign or inflammatory processes.

rejected.why: Aggressive chronic otitis media typically lacks intracranial extension and profound sensorineural loss; imaging enhancement pattern is less specific.
Adenocarcinoma is a specific subtype without histologic support; squamous carcinoma (included in middle ear cancer) is far more common.
Granulomatosis with polyangiitis usually has systemic features and ANCA positivity; isolated destructive ear lesion is atypical.
Cholesteatoma can erode bone but usually shows non-enhancing soft tissue and less often causes profound sensorineural loss or intracranial extension.
Necrotizing otitis externa typically affects elderly diabetics and is limited to external canal; here middle ear and intracranial involvement are present.
